title: Reject row-0 peel + `[{` fuse in `write_json_to_buf`
impact: Tested whether peeling row 0 out of `write_json_to_buf`'s row loop (fusing the leading `[` with row 0's `{` into one 2-byte prelude, short-circuiting empty results, and dropping the per-iteration `if (row_index > 0)` branch) would move any measurable selectBytes lane. Two order-flipped passes of `select_bytes_repeated_calls.dart` reproduced small candidate-faster deltas on 10/100 rows (about -1% to -2%) but stayed inside the harness ~3% effect floor; the 1000-row lane collapsed from -1.5% to -0.2% (drift-suspected) and the 1-row × 8-int lane trended candidate-slower on both passes (+0.4%, +4.6%). One pass of `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` showed the load-bearing 10k × 8 int lane at +5.7% on pair 1, a run-to-run drift signature rather than a real regression. Rejected: the per-row branch is well-predicted and the bracket fuse is byte-count noise, so the reproduced 1-2% wins do not offset the ~60-line encoder-body macro that shares row-0 and row-N cell encoding. Runtime prototype preserved at `archive/exp-223`.
